gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-hanuman: Hanuman is a classic serif with a high-waisted lowercase and refined manners. Happy Monkey stands over it in bold display letters, ruler-straight in weight, with wide gaps in the e, and the two look clearly unrelated.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-kadwa: Happy Monkey draws every stroke at a ruler-straight weight, like bent tubing with a loud, distinctive streak. Then Kadwa, a classic serif with open-ended curves and a tall lowercase, brings an editorial steadiness that makes the heading look even more playful.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-noticia-text: Happy Monkey brings bold, ruler-straight strokes and wide gaps in the e, with a lowercase of moderate height. Noticia Text is the literary one, its lowercase filling most of the letter height.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla reads refined and authoritative, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals and its e pried open like a clasp. But Happy Monkey is the louder voice, and if it were shrunk small, its bold display character would fade against that text serif.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-pridi: Refined and classic, Pridi gives its small letters an almost capital-sized stance. Happy Monkey's ruler-straight strokes sit beside it, and a long run of Pridi's serif text feels spacious, with generous gaps where curves meet stems.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-scope-one: Happy Monkey is bold and distinctive, with an unshaded, steady outline and wide gaps in the e. And Scope One, a classic serif with stubby ascenders and spilling counters, gives the strongest quality of the pair: a loud display face meeting a traditional, refined body.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-slabo-13px: Chunky, bold and a bit goofy. Happy Monkey has a rounded-nib look and wide gaps in the e, while Slabo 13px gives the serif body large open counters, so a modest size suggestion works fine for its bookish, dignified text.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-suwannaphum: Happy Monkey sets a bold, distinctive tone, its stroke edges running parallel through every curve. Suwannaphum is the dignified, editorial serif that follows, with a very open c and a high x-height that would make a longer passage feel airy and substantial.
gen-gf-hi-melody-fs-amulya: Glyphs huddle together like pressed tiles in Hi Melody, hand-drawn and inviting. It brings casual personality, while Amulya, a contemporary sans, keeps its curves generously open and does the quieter work of being read.
gen-gf-hi-melody-fs-bespoke-sans: Sharp and refined, Bespoke Sans leaves generous space between curve ends and the stem, so its letters look crisp. Hi Melody handles personality with a hand-drawn feel, while the body is better for brief copy.
